title: Calculate cell type scores and assign cell types
text: Prepare seurat object: See also https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial.html#setup--seurat-object  Compared manual marked cell types: See also https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial.html#assigning-cell-type-identity--clusters
code: suppressWarnings(SeuratData::InstallData("pbmc3k")) pbmc <- pbmc3k.SeuratData::pbmc3k pbmc <- Seurat::UpdateSeuratObject(pbmc) pbmc[["percent.mt"]] <- Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet(pbmc, pattern = "^MT-") pbmc <- subset(pbmc, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 2500 & percent.mt < 5) pbmc <- Seurat::NormalizeData(pbmc) pbmc <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(pbmc, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000) pbmc <- Seurat::ScaleData(pbmc, features = rownames(pbmc)) pbmc <- Seurat::RunPCA(pbmc, features = Seurat::VariableFeatures(object = pbmc)) pbmc <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:10) pbmc <- Seurat::FindClusters(pbmc, resolution = 0.5) #> Modularity Optimizer version 1.3.0 by Ludo Waltman and Nees Jan van Eck #>  #> Number of nodes: 2638 #> Number of edges: 95927 #>  #> Running Louvain algorithm... #> Maximum modularity in 10 random starts: 0.8728 #> Number of communities: 9 #> Elapsed time: 0 seconds pbmc <- Seurat::RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:10) library(hitype)  markers <- data.frame(     cellName = c(         "Naive CD4+ T", "CD14+ Mono", "Memory CD4+", "B",         "CD8+ T", "FCFR3A+ Mono", "NK", "DC", "Platelet"     ),     geneSymbolmore1 = c(         "IL7R,CCR7",  "CD14,LYZ", "IL7R,S100A4", "MS4A1",         "CD8A", "FCGR3A,MS4A7", "GNLY,NKG7", "FCER1A,CST3", "PPBP"     ),     geneSymbolmore2 = rep("", 9) )  # Load gene sets gs <- gs_prepare(markers)  # Assign cell types obj <- RunHitype(pbmc, gs)  Seurat::DimPlot(obj, group.by = "hitype", label = TRUE, label.box = TRUE) +   Seurat::NoLegend()

what: Using hitype_score and hitype_assign on Seurat directly
title: Calculate cell type scores and assign cell types
text: default, hitype_score() expects log-normalized data (scaled = FALSE) performs z-scoring. Seurat v5, access normalized data Seurat::GetAssayData(pbmc, layer = "data"): prefer pass pre-scaled data (e.g. Seurat scale.data layer), use scaled = TRUE: scoring learned weights (see vignette("train-marker-weights")), use norm = "weight", use_sensitivity = FALSE scores normalized total marker weight shared markers double-penalized: compare manual marked cell types: See: https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial.html#assigning-cell-type-identity--clusters
code: scores <- hitype_score(Seurat::GetAssayData(pbmc, layer = "data"), gs) cell_types <- hitype_assign(pbmc$seurat_clusters, scores, gs) summary(cell_types) #> # A tibble: 9 × 5 #>   Level Cluster CellType      Score  Margin #>   <int> <fct>   <chr>         <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1     1 0       Naive CD4+ T  0.721  0.685  #> 2     1 1       CD14+ Mono    2.28   1.20   #> 3     1 2       Memory CD4+   0.599  0.0927 #> 4     1 3       B             2.09   2.17   #> 5     1 4       NK            1.43   0.179  #> 6     1 5       FCFR3A+ Mono  3.42   2.44   #> 7     1 6       NK            3.91   2.88   #> 8     1 7       DC            5.55   4.59   #> 9     1 8       Platelet     11.5   11.3 scores <- hitype_score(Seurat::GetAssayData(pbmc, layer = "scale.data"),                        gs, scaled = TRUE) scores <- hitype_score(Seurat::GetAssayData(pbmc, layer = "data"), gs,                        norm = "weight", use_sensitivity = FALSE)

title: Prepare gene sets
text: Besides wide ScType format , gs_prepare() also accepts universal marker format — long table one row per (cell type, marker) pair, used across author’s biopipen tools. also default output train_weights() find_markers(). table can data.frame file (.txt/.tsv, .csv, .xlsx, .rds, .qs/.qs2 qs2 package installed) following columns: cell_type (required): Cell type name. gene (required): Marker gene. direction (optional): positive negative (aliases pos/neg/+/-, case-insensitive). Negative markers penalize cell type. weight (optional): Numeric magnitude marker weight. Combined direction: positive marker gets weight abs(weight), negative marker gets -abs(weight). direction missing, signed weight used -. neither given, marker gets weight 1. Zero-weight markers allowed. tissue (optional): Tissue type. One can pass tissue_type gs_prepare() filter gene sets tissue type. species, cancer (optional): Reserved filter columns (accepted ignored gs_prepare()). level (optional): Cell type level, ScType format . Column names matched case-insensitively alias (celltype/type → cell_type; marker/gene_symbol → gene; sign → direction; tissueType → tissue).
code: markers <- data.frame(     cell_type = rep(c("CD4 T", "CD8 T"), each = 3),     gene = c("CD3E", "CD4", "IL7R", "CD3E", "CD8A", "CD8B"),     direction = c("positive", "positive", "negative", "positive", "positive", "positive"),     weight = c(2.0, 1.5, 0.5, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0) ) gs <- gs_prepare(markers) gs$gene_sets[[1]]$`CD4 T` #> $markers #> [1] "CD3E" "CD4"  "IL7R" #>  #> $weights #> [1]  2.0  1.5 -0.5

what: Preparing your own gene sets (wide ScType format)
title: Prepare gene sets
text: can also prepare gene sets wide ScType format. gene sets data.frame tab-delimited file following columns: tissueType (optional): Tissue type. One can pass tissue_type gs_prepare() filter gene sets tissue type. cellName (required): Cell type name. geneSymbolmore1 (required): Markers cell type. Multiple markers separated ,. One can use suffix + indicate marker positive marker, - indicate marker negative marker. Multiple +’s allowed indicate marker strong positive marker. Multiple -’s allowed indicate marker strong negative marker. example, CD3E+++ indicates CD3E strong positive marker, CD14--- indicates CD14 strong negative marker. geneSymbolmore2 (required): Negative markers cell type. column can empty strings. kept compatibility ScType. suffixes allowed column. marker column marker previous column suffix -. level (optional): Cell type level. level cellName. must start 1 increase 1. final cell type consists one cellName level. format cellName1,cellName2;cellName3,cellName4;... cellName current level. example, CD4 level 1, nextLevels Naive;Activated indicates CD4 followed Naive level 2 Activated level 3. nextLevels also specified Naive level 2, cellName level 3 CD4 intersection Activated cellNames level 3 Naive limited nextLevels Naive. level nextLevels empty, cellNames level cellNames next level limited nextLevels level. ! can used indicate cellNames next level excluded. example, !Naive indicates Naive excluded cellNames next level. ! character level, cellNames level excluded. data.frame markers (e.g. output train_weights()) can passed directly gs_prepare():
code: markers <- data.frame(     cellName = c("CD4 T", "CD8 T"),     geneSymbolmore1 = c("CD3E,CD4,IL7R", "CD3E,CD8A,CD8B"),     geneSymbolmore2 = c("", "") ) gs <- gs_prepare(markers)

what: Finding markers from your own data
title: Train marker weights
text: find_markers() discovers marker genes labeled dataset (e.g. pbmc$seurat_clusters) returns directly universal marker format consumed gs_prepare() (pass format = "db" legacy wide ScType-style format), dependency-light fold-change (fc, default), Seurat, presto backends: See ?find_markers details.
code: markers <- find_markers(pbmc, clusters = pbmc$seurat_clusters, method = "fc") weights <- train_weights(path_to_gs = markers, exprs = pbmc, method = "glmnet") gs <- gs_prepare(weights)

title: Prepare gene sets for hitype — gs_prepare
text: path_to_db_file data frame markers path marker file. Two formats supported auto-detected: hitype/ScType db format (data.frame tab-delimited text excel file following columns): tissueType: tissue type cell type annotated. column required tissue_type specified. cellName: name cell type annotated. nextLevels: Possible next levels cell type annotated. Introduced hitype, can work hierarchical cell. Levels separated ;. Cell names level separated ,. exclamatory mark ! beginning level means cell names level mutually exclusive. levels less possible next levels, remaining levels possible next levels. See example . geneSymbolmore1: gene symbols marker genes expected expressed cell type annotated. genes can suffixed one +. + means higher expression level. example, CD3E++ means gene CD3E expected highly expressed cell type. geneSymbolmore2: gene symbols marker genes expected expressed cell type annotated. level: levels cell names. Introduced hitype, can work hierarchical cell names. Different levels cellNames predicted separately. example, CD4 level 1 Naive level 2, prediction cell type CD4 Naive. levels start 1 consecutive. universal marker format (see https://pwwang.github.io/biopipen/api/biopipen.ns.scrna/), long table one row per gene per cell type: cell_type (required): cell type. gene (required): marker gene. direction: positive negative (aliases: pos/neg/+/-, case-insensitive). Optional. Defaults positive. weight: numeric weight. Optional. Defaults 1. positive marker gets abs(weight); negative marker gets -abs(weight). direction given, weight used -(signed weights accepted). tissue, species, cancer: optional, filtering tissue_type. level: optional. levels start 1 consecutive. Column names case-insensitive aliases supported: celltype/cellType/Type cell_type, marker/gene_symbol gene, sign direction, tissueType tissue. Text files extensions txt/tsv/csv/xlsx/xls read tables; rds/qs/qs2 files contain data.frame (qs/qs2 require qs2 package installed). tissue_type tissue type cell type annotated. db format, requires tissueType column marker gene database file; universal format, tissue column (alias tissueType). tissue_type specified, cell types specified tissue type used annotation. tissue_type specified, cell types marker gene database file used annotation. weight_encoding encoding weights. default, plus (+) positive weight; minus (-) negative weight star (*) zero weight. sign indicates 1. One plus indicates 2, etc. can use function encode values. example function(x) x*x make weights squared involved computation.

code: list(      gene_sets = list(          # level 1          list( CD4 = list(markers = c(...), weights = c(...)), ... ),          # level 2          list( Naive = list(markers = c(...), weights = c(...)), ... )      ),      # All possible final cell names      cell_names = list(CD4 = list(Naive = c("Activated", "Proliferating")))   )

title: Prepare gene sets for hitype — gs_prepare
code: # nextLevels example # If we have the following cell types: #   level  cellName  nextLevels #   1      CD4       Naive,Memory #   2      Naive #   2      Memory #   3      Activated #   3      Proliferating # Then possible final cell names are: #   CD4 Naive Activated #   CD4 Naive Proliferating #   CD4 Memory Activated #   CD4 Memory Proliferating # # If the `nextLevels` of CD4 is `!Naive`, then possible final cell names are: #   CD4 Memory Activated #   CD4 Memory Proliferating # # If the `nextLevels` of CD4 is `!`, then possible final cell names are: #   CD4 Activated #   CD4 Proliferating # # If the `nextLevels` of CD4 is `!Naive;!`, then possible final cell names # are: #   CD4 Memory  # A gene set in the universal marker format: markers <- data.frame(     cell_type = c("CD4", "CD4", "CD8", "CD8", "CD8"),     gene = c("CD4", "IL7R", "CD8A", "CD8B", "GZMB"),     direction = c("positive", "positive", "positive", "positive", "negative"),     weight = c(2, 1, 3, 1, 1) ) gs <- gs_prepare(markers) gs$gene_sets[[1]]$CD4 #> $markers #> [1] "CD4"  "IL7R" #>  #> $weights #> [1] 2 1 #>  gs$gene_sets[[1]]$CD8 #> $markers #> [1] "CD8A" "CD8B" "GZMB" #>  #> $weights #> [1]  3  1 -1 #>

Simple, interpretable. "lr" Logistic regression coefficients (one-vs-rest). Classic ML approach. Use cv_folds stability. "glmnet" Sparse logistic regression elastic net penalty (alpha = 0.5). Automatically zeros uninformative markers. Recommended users. Requires glmnet package. "rf" Random forest permutation importance. Captures non-linear marker interactions. Requires ranger package. "xgb" XGBoost gain-based feature importance. State---art tree method. Requires xgboost package. "lrp" Neural network + Layer-wise Relevance Propagation. Deep learning approach. title: Version 0.0.6
text: ✨ gs_prepare() now auto-detects universal marker format (long table cell_type gene columns, shared biopipen’s CellTypeAnnotation) addition native wide ScType-style format. Column aliases matched case-insensitively (celltype/type → cell_type; marker/gene_symbol → gene; sign → direction; tissueType → tissue). Optional columns: direction (positive/negative, aliases pos/neg/+/-), weight (numeric; positive markers get abs(weight), negative markers get -abs(weight), signed weights used -direction missing), tissue (filtered tissue_type), level. Marker files can .txt/.tsv, .csv, .xlsx, .rds, .qs/.qs2 (latter qs/qs2 package installed). ✨ train_weights() find_markers() gain format argument ("universal" default, "db" legacy wide format), internal compile_weights(). default universal output carries exact numeric weights — legacy db format’s weight-suffix magnitude shift longer applies default flow, including run_weights_on_test_data.

title: Version 0.0.5
text: ✨ Add find_markers() discover marker genes data dependency-light fc (default), Seurat, presto backends, directly producing db data.frame consumable gs_prepare(). ✨ Add method argument train_weights() 7 weight-learning backends: uniform, correlation, lr, glmnet (default, recommended), rf, xgb, lrp. epochs batch_size now apply lrp method . ✨ Add cv_folds argument cross-validated weight estimation: stratified folds, per-fold weights averaged stability. Used lr, glmnet, lrp. norm = "weight" normalizes scores sum(abs(weights)) (fairer across cell types different marker numbers); use_sensitivity = FALSE disables marker-sensitivity weighting — recommended scoring learned weights avoid double-penalizing shared markers. 🔧 Statistical soundness: removed input masking prepare_data_for_training() (masked zeros let model learn mask pattern instead expression). 🔧 Seurat v5 compatibility: use Seurat::GetAssayData(x, layer = "data") instead direct @assays$RNA@data / @assays$RNA@scale.data access. 🧩 New suggested dependencies: glmnet, ranger, xgboost (required per method, optional overall).
